enzyme_name: D-lysergyl peptide synthetase (LPS1 trimodular NRPS, acting with LPS2)
organism_context: Ergot fungi: Claviceps purpurea, Claviceps fusiformis, Epichloe/Neotyphodium spp.
distinct_activities: cyclol-forming chain release by the C-terminal condensation-like domain
rationale: Ergotamine assembly is run by a nonribosomal peptide synthetase in which LPS1 (LpsA) is one ~370 kDa polypeptide carrying three complete modules (three adenylation, three condensation plus thiolation domains) and a C-terminal condensation-like domain that performs the cyclol cyclization/release, so that single chain holds many distinct catalytic activities; D-lysergic acid is activated by the separate polypeptide LPS2 (LpsB), i.e. the full catalyst is a two-subunit complex and only LPS1 itself is a fused multidomain enzyme.
direction_note: The NRPS runs only in the condensation (ergotamine-forming) direction and is driven by ATP hydrolysis at four adenylation steps; ModelSEED's equation omits ATP entirely, which is exactly why the biosynthetic direction scores as endergonic and gets flipped to a nonexistent ergotamine hydrolysis.

enzyme_name: CYP83B1 (aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; SUR2/RNT1)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana and other Brassicales (benzylglucosinolate branch, PWY-2821)
rationale: CYP83B1 is the oxime-metabolizing P450 of the glucosinolate pathway and oxidizes aromatic aldoximes such as (Z)-phenylacetaldoxime to the activated aci-nitro/nitrile-oxide species; it is a single-activity microsomal monooxygenase that works with a separate NADPH:cytochrome P450 reductase polypeptide, which is a partner protein and not a fused second catalytic domain.
direction_note: The real reaction is an O2- and NADPH-consuming P450 oxidation of the aldoxime; ModelSEED's entry has dropped O2 and rewritten it as an NADP+-linked dehydrogenation (leaving one oxygen and two charges unbalanced), so the thermodynamic sign that drives the '<' call is meaningless - the enzyme only ever converts aldoxime to nitrile oxide.

enzyme_name: CYP83B1 (indole-3-acetaldoxime N-oxidizing cytochrome P450; SUR2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, indole glucosinolate branch (PWY-601); CYP83B1 is the high-affinity enzyme for indole-3-acetaldoxime
rationale: Hansen et al. showed directly that CYP83B1 is the oxime-metabolizing enzyme that oxidizes indole-3-acetaldoxime in the glucosinolate pathway, and Naur et al. confirmed CYP83A1/CYP83B1 are nonredundant with CYP83B1 specific for the indole/aromatic oximes; it carries a single monooxygenase activity.
direction_note: O2 is missing from the ModelSEED equation and NADPH sits on the wrong side, converting an irreversible P450 oxidation into an apparent NADP+-linked dehydrogenation; the enzyme only runs aldoxime to nitrile oxide.

enzyme_name: CYP83A1 (aliphatic aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; REF2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, homomethionine-derived aliphatic glucosinolate branch (PWY-1187)
rationale: CYP83A1 is the nonredundant P450 that oxidizes the methylthioalkyl aldoximes of the chain-elongated methionine branch (ref2 mutants lose aliphatic glucosinolates), a single monooxygenase activity dependent on a separate NADPH:P450 reductase.
direction_note: O2 has been dropped and the reaction rewritten as an NADP+-linked dehydrogenation, so the thermodynamics behind ModelSEED's '<' do not describe the real P450 chemistry, which runs only toward the nitrile oxide.

enzyme_name: CYP83A1 (aliphatic aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; REF2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, dihomomethionine-derived glucosinolate branch (PWYQT-4471)
rationale: Same single-activity P450 monooxygenase as the other methylthioalkyl aldoximes of the chain-elongated branch; CYP83A1 was shown to be the aliphatic-oxime-metabolizing enzyme, with no second catalytic domain.
direction_note: O2 omitted and NADPH placed on the product side; the enzymatic flux is strictly aldoxime to nitrile oxide.

enzyme_name: CYP83A1 (aliphatic aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; REF2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, trihomomethionine-derived glucosinolate branch (PWYQT-4472)
rationale: Assigned to CYP83A1 as the aliphatic oxime-metabolizing P450 of this chain-elongated series (pathway-level annotation; the longer-chain homologues were not individually assayed); a P450 monooxygenase with one catalytic activity.
direction_note: O2 omitted and NADPH on the wrong side; the oxidation to the nitrile oxide is the only direction the P450 runs.

enzyme_name: CYP83A1 (aliphatic aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; REF2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, tetrahomomethionine-derived glucosinolate branch (PWYQT-4473)
rationale: Same CYP83A1 monooxygenase step of the chain-elongated aliphatic branch, inferred from the pathway series rather than from an assay on this specific C7 aldoxime; single catalytic activity.
direction_note: O2 omitted and NADPH on the wrong side; only the aldoxime-oxidizing direction is enzymatically real.

enzyme_name: CYP83A1 (aliphatic aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; REF2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, pentahomomethionine-derived glucosinolate branch (PWYQT-4474)
rationale: CYP83A1 is the annotated oxime oxidase for the whole methylthioalkyl aldoxime series; a P450 monooxygenase with a single catalytic activity (its reductase partner is a separate protein).
direction_note: O2 omitted and NADPH on the wrong side, so the '<' call rests on an equation that is not the P450 chemistry.

enzyme_name: CYP83A1 (aliphatic aldoxime-metabolizing cytochrome P450; REF2)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, hexahomomethionine-derived glucosinolate branch (PWYQT-4475)
rationale: Longest-chain member of the same CYP83A1-catalysed aldoxime oxidation series; assignment is by pathway analogy, and the enzyme is a one-activity P450 monooxygenase.
direction_note: O2 omitted and NADPH on the product side; the enzyme only oxidizes the aldoxime.

enzyme_name: manganese-oxidizing multicopper oxidase MnxG (catalytic subunit of the MnxEFG 'Mnx' complex)
organism_context: Bacillus sp. PL-12 and SG-1 spores (Mnx); alternative animal-heme-peroxidase route (MopA) in Erythrobacter sp. SD-21 and Aurantimonas
rationale: Mn(III) oxidation to Mn(IV)O2 is carried out by the multicopper oxidase Mnx, which performs both one-electron oxidations Mn(II)->Mn(III) and Mn(III)->Mn(IV) at the same type-1/trinuclear copper machinery - one oxidase activity applied twice, not two activities; Mnx is a multi-subunit MnxE/MnxF/MnxG complex, so by the complex exclusion the catalytic MnxG subunit is scored monofunctional.
direction_note: The equation is balanced and is a genuine O2-coupled multicopper-oxidase half-reaction; biologically Mn(III) is only ever oxidized to MnO2 (and abiotic Mn(III) disproportionation also goes that way), so ModelSEED's reductive '<' is not a reaction anything runs.

enzyme_name: phytochelatin synthase 1 (AtPCS1/CAD1), acting as a glutathione-S-conjugate carboxypeptidase (deglycinase)
organism_context: Arabidopsis thaliana, camalexin biosynthesis from GS-IAN (CAMALEXIN-SYN)
rationale: Removal of glycine from the glutathione-indole-3-acetonitrile conjugate is attributed to phytochelatin synthase (PCS1), a papain-like cysteine enzyme; although PCS1 can both transpeptidate (phytochelatin synthesis) and hydrolyse GS-conjugates, both proceed through the same single catalytic Cys acyl-enzyme with water or an amine as acceptor, so this is one active site rather than two fused catalytic domains - an unidentified carboxypeptidase remains a possible alternative catalyst.
direction_note: A peptide-bond hydrolysis that releases free glycine is effectively irreversible; ModelSEED's '<' would require ATP-free re-ligation of glycine onto the gamma-Glu-Cys conjugate, which no enzyme does.

enzyme_name: streptothricin hydrolase SttH (isochorismatase-like 'cysteine hydrolase' family)
organism_context: Streptomyces spp.; SttH inactivates streptothricin antibiotics, and N-methylation of the streptolidine lactam (orf6 of the BD-12 cluster) confers partial resistance to it
rationale: SttH hydrolyses the streptolidine lactam ring of streptothricins to the corresponding ring-opened acid, matching this reaction (EC 3.5.2.-); it is a single-domain isochorismatase-like hydrolase whose activity depends on one conserved catalytic cysteine, with no second catalytic activity reported.
direction_note: Lactam hydrolysis is an irreversible inactivation step; the reverse (intramolecular amide formation from the free acid) would need activation chemistry absent from this equation.

enzyme_name: unidentified - conversion of alpha-3',4'-anhydrovinblastine to vinblastine (hydration at C3'-C4')
organism_context: Catharanthus roseus, vindoline/vinblastine pathway (PWY-5292); the preceding coupling of catharanthine and vindoline to anhydrovinblastine is done by the class III peroxidase CrPrx1, but no enzyme has been assigned to the anhydrovinblastine -> vinblastine step
rationale: No protein has been shown to catalyse the net hydration of anhydrovinblastine to vinblastine; in heterologous reconstructions of the pathway the final conversion is performed chemically, so neither an enzyme identity nor its domain architecture can be stated.
direction_note: The only flux ever observed is biosynthetic (anhydrovinblastine to vinblastine), so ModelSEED's dehydrating '<' is backwards, but because no catalyst is known the call rests on pathway flux rather than on enzymology.

enzyme_name: FR-008/candicidin modular type I polyketide synthase (FscA-FscD megasynthases, PABA-CoA starter)
organism_context: Streptomyces sp. FR-008 / Streptomyces griseus candicidin producers
distinct_activities: acyl carrier protein phosphopantetheinyl acyl transfer (ACP)
rationale: The polyketide chain is built by the FR-008/candicidin PKS, whose individual polypeptides (FscA-FscD) each fuse many catalytic domains (KS, AT, DH, ER, KR, ACP, TE) on one chain, which is polyfunctional in the strict sense; the complete conversion is nevertheless distributed over several such megasynthases.
direction_note: The entry collapses ~20 malonyl-CoA/methylmalonyl-CoA extensions and their NADPH reductions into 'PABA-CoA -> FR-008-III', so every atom of the polyketide backbone and the decarboxylative driving force are missing; the biosynthetic direction is nonetheless the only one that exists.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous addition of L-ascorbate to indol-3-ylmethyl isothiocyanate (ascorbigen formation)
organism_context: Brassicaceae tissue after myrosinase-mediated glucobrassicin hydrolysis; also occurs in vitro and in fermented/processed cabbage
rationale: Ascorbigen arises non-enzymatically when the unstable glucobrassicin-derived indol-3-ylmethyl isothiocyanate reacts with ascorbate, releasing thiocyanate; there is no catalysing protein to classify.
direction_note: This is a spontaneous chemical trapping reaction with no enzyme and no reverse route - ascorbigen is a stable end product, so ModelSEED's '<' (regenerating the reactive isothiocyanate from ascorbigen plus thiocyanate) does not occur.

enzyme_name: 15-cis-phytoene desaturase (PDS, plant/cyanobacterial type; 15-cis-phytoene:plastoquinone oxidoreductase)
organism_context: Plants, algae and cyanobacteria (oxygenic phototrophs); PDS is the target of norflurazon and related bleaching herbicides
rationale: PDS is a single FAD-dependent desaturase that introduces one double bond per catalytic cycle using plastoquinone as electron acceptor; the fact that it performs two successive desaturations (phytoene->phytofluene->zeta-carotene) is the same activity acting twice, not a second catalytic function.
direction_note: The desaturation is physiologically irreversible and is pulled further by PTOX reoxidation of plastoquinol; ModelSEED's '<' would mean hydrogenating phytofluene back to phytoene, which PDS does not do.

enzyme_name: 15-cis-phytoene desaturase (PDS), second desaturation step (phytofluene -> 9,15,9'-tri-cis-zeta-carotene)
organism_context: Plants, algae and cyanobacteria; same enzyme as the preceding phytoene desaturation
rationale: The same PDS polypeptide carries out this second plastoquinone-dependent desaturation; one catalytic activity applied to the successive substrate, with no second fused catalytic domain.
direction_note: Carotene desaturation runs only in the oxidative direction in vivo, so the '<' (reduction by plastoquinol) is not an enzymatic possibility.

enzyme_name: cellobiohydrolase (cellulose 1,4-beta-cellobiosidase, reducing-end acting; GH7 Cel7A/CBHI type)
organism_context: Cellulolytic fungi (Trichoderma reesei/Hypocrea jecorina TrCel7A, Aspergillus, Rasamsonia) and bacteria
rationale: A processive glycoside hydrolase that releases cellobiose from the reducing end of cello-oligosaccharides; its carbohydrate-binding module is a non-catalytic targeting domain, so the enzyme carries only one catalytic activity.
direction_note: Cellotetraose hydrolysis should give two cellobiose, but the entry writes only one, so the equation is missing a whole product; glycoside-bond hydrolysis is strongly exergonic and irreversible, making ModelSEED's condensing '<' wrong regardless.

enzyme_name: 4-alpha-glucanotransferase / disproportionating enzyme 1 (DPE1; amylomaltase MalQ in bacteria), EC 2.4.1.25
organism_context: Arabidopsis and other plant chloroplasts (starch degradation II, PWY-6724); MalQ in E. coli maltose metabolism
rationale: DPE1 is a single-activity transglycosylase that disproportionates malto-oligosaccharides (2 maltotriose -> maltopentaose + glucose), transferring a maltosyl unit rather than hydrolysing; it has one catalytic domain and no second activity.
direction_note: The entry keeps only 'maltotriose -> glucose' and has lost the second maltotriose and the maltopentaose product; the underlying transglycosylation has a near-zero free-energy change and is genuinely reversible, with net direction set by the oligosaccharide pools (degradative in the chloroplast at night), so neither '<' nor '>' is an enzymatic property.

enzyme_name: SpnS, SAM-dependent dTDP-D-forosamine N,N-dimethyltransferase
organism_context: Saccharopolyspora spinosa, spinosyn/dTDP-D-forosamine pathway (PWY-6808); forosamine methyltransferase homologues also in auricin producers
rationale: In vitro reconstitution of TDP-D-forosamine biosynthesis identified SpnS as the SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase that installs both N-methyl groups, i.e. one methyltransferase activity used twice on the 4-amino sugar; no second catalytic function is reported.
direction_note: SAM-dependent methyl transfer is strongly exergonic and physiologically unidirectional; ModelSEED's '<' would require SAH-driven demethylation, which this enzyme does not catalyse.

enzyme_name: rutinosidase (rutin beta-diglycosidase; 'rutinase'), releases rutinose in one step
organism_context: Fungi (Aspergillus niger K2 rutinosidase, Penicillium) and plants (Tartary buckwheat FtGH1)
rationale: Rutinosidases are single-domain glycoside hydrolases (GH5/GH3-type diglycosidases) that cleave the glycosidic bond between quercetin and the intact rutinose disaccharide; their transglycosylation capability uses the same active site and acyl/glycosyl-enzyme intermediate, so it is not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Glycoside hydrolysis in dilute aqueous cell sap is effectively irreversible, so the enzymology supports rutin breakdown rather than ModelSEED's '<' synthesis of rutin from quercetin plus free rutinose.

enzyme_name: DmdC, 3-methylmercaptopropionyl-CoA (MMPA-CoA) dehydrogenase, an acyl-CoA dehydrogenase family flavoenzyme
organism_context: Marine Roseobacters and SAR11 (Ruegeria pomeroyi DSS-3, Pelagibacter), DMSP demethylation pathway
rationale: DmdC is a straightforward acyl-CoA dehydrogenase homologue carrying out the alpha,beta-desaturation of 3-methylmercaptopropionyl-CoA with its tightly bound FAD; it is a homo-oligomer of one catalytic activity, not a fused multi-activity chain.
direction_note: Acyl-CoA dehydrogenases reoxidize their FAD through electron-transfer flavoprotein and the quinone pool, not through free FAD/FADH2; writing free FAD/FADH2 as the couple makes the oxidation look reversible and is what lets the '<' (reductive) direction win on thermodynamics.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous hydration of NADH to (6S)-NAD(P)H-hydrate (the enzymatic repair reaction instead needs ATP-dependent NAXD/NnrD dehydratase)
organism_context: Universal; NADH hydration is a spontaneous damage reaction repaired by the conserved NAD(P)HX dehydratase (ATP- or ADP-dependent) in bacteria, plants and animals
rationale: This MetaCyc/Rhea entry carries no EC number and no ATP, which identifies it as the spontaneous (non-enzymatic) hydration leg of the NADH repair pathway rather than the enzymatic dehydration; the genuine repair enzyme NAXD/NnrD is a separate ATP-dependent dehydratase (in many bacteria fused to the NnrE epimerase, but that fusion is not what this entry describes).
direction_note: Uncatalysed, the only thing that happens is hydration of NADH to NADHX (the damage direction, '>'); the reverse needs ATP hydrolysis coupled by NAXD, and that ATP is absent from this equation, so ModelSEED's '<' describes a reaction that cannot run as written.

enzyme_name: none - spontaneous hydration of NADH to (6R)-NAD(P)H-hydrate (repair of the 6R epimer additionally requires the NAXE/NnrE epimerase before NAXD can act)
organism_context: Universal; the (6R) epimer is handled by NAD(P)HX epimerase (NAXE), which feeds the (6S) epimer to the ATP-dependent dehydratase
rationale: As written (NADHX = NADH + H2O with no EC number and no ATP) this is the spontaneous hydration producing the (6R) epimer; no enzyme dehydrates (6R)-NADHX directly - it must first be epimerised by NAXE - so there is no catalysing protein to classify for this entry.
direction_note: The spontaneous drift is NADH -> (6R)-NADHX; recovery of NADH from this epimer takes two enzymes (NAXE epimerase then ATP-dependent NAXD dehydratase), neither of which is represented here, so the '<' direction is unreachable with this equation.

enzyme_name: LmbJ, SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase of lincomycin biosynthesis
organism_context: Streptomyces lincolnensis (lincomycin A); homologue CcbJ in the celesticetin producer Streptomyces caelestis
rationale: The final N-methylation of N-demethyllincomycin to lincomycin A is performed by the SAM-dependent methyltransferase LmbJ (CcbJ in the celesticetin pathway), a single-activity small-molecule methyltransferase acting on the 4-propyl-proline nitrogen.
direction_note: SAM-to-SAH methyl transfer is essentially irreversible, so the enzymology supports the methylating '>' direction and not ModelSEED's '<'.
